bug_semantics: phpseclib ASN1::decodeOID()/_decodeOID() BER-decodes attacker-controlled Object Identifier content from untrusted ASN.1 (X.509 certs, PKCS#8 keys, etc.) by accumulating each base-128 septet into a Math_BigInteger via per-byte leftShift(7)/OR and then implode()/stringifying the arcs. A long single sub-identifier (or many such OIDs) amplifies a few kilobytes of DER into huge integers and decimal strings, consuming CPU and memory (CWE-400 DoS). CVE-2024-27355 added an OpenJDK-copied 4096-byte cap that is still large enough for PHP BigInteger DoS; the 2026 fix lowers the cap to 128 bytes.
flaw_origin: The amplification mechanism was first written in e793461543d16a5d52f8805882bf6d45bf8c6cde (2019-04-30, 'ASN1: revamp how OIDs are handled'), which replaced the old native-integer septet loop inside OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding with a new unbounded _decodeOID() BigInteger implementation and no length check. That is the smallest first-write of the named decodeOID() path. e32531001b4d62c66c3d824ccef54ffad835eb59 (2024-02-24) later added if ($len > 4096) return false as the CVE-2024-27355 mitigation; that cap is an incomplete patch of the same algorithm, not a new BIC. d53d2021bcb9f6a04d5d44ec99e6bbef219a71bc only tightens 4096 to 128.

reasoning: CVE-2026-44167 is a real CWE-400 DoS: loading untrusted ASN.1 exercises ASN1::decodeOID()/_decodeOID(), which expands attacker-chosen OID bytes through BigInteger arithmetic and decimal stringification. CVE.org is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn), so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. The 2026 patch d53d2021 only lowers the OID content cap from 4096 to 128 bytes; that is the fix SHA, and it is the same object that first lands on 1.0/2.0 and is merged into 3.0 (present in 1.0.29, 2.0.54, 3.0.52; absent from the last affected tags). The 4096 cap itself was introduced by e3253100 as the CVE-2024-27355 mitigation and is an incomplete bound on an already-expensive decoder, not the first write of the vulnerable lines. git log -S/_L and parent-tree inspection show the named decodeOID mechanism first appears in e7934615: parent 756b2474 still uses a native-integer septet loop with no _decodeOID, and e7934615 is a single-parent non-merge, non-squash first-write of unbounded Math_BigInteger OID decoding. 3.0's namespaced decodeOID is a later port/merge of that same algorithm (present unbounded in 3.0.0), which is a refactor/merge and therefore not a BIC. Advisory version floors start at major-line beginnings and over-approximate (0.1.1 predates ASN.1 support); the precise introducing tags are 1.0.16 / 2.0.16 / 3.0.0, which still contain e7934615 before the patched boundary.
